The Challenge

One roof for a company that ships in pieces.

B&R's 2019 calendar ran across five separate industry shows: ATX West, Automation & Power World, the CSIA conference, the Automation World Expo, PACK EXPO, each one borrowing a slice of the sales and engineering team for a few days at a time.

AutomationCON was the one event on that calendar B&R owned outright: a self-hosted, multi-day conference built to do in four days what the trade-show circuit could only do in fragments. Get regional sales managers aligned, put engineers in front of the newest hardware, and give partners and prospects a controlled room to ask real questions about real machines.

That meant running five distinct programs (a leadership meeting, an executive roundtable, a general session, hands-on engineering workshops, and a full trade showcase), plus a full slate of evening entertainment, inside one resort property, on one shared budget, with one specialist threading it all together.

Three months out, a highway fire closed a major interstate artery between the Atlanta airport and Lake Lanier Islands. Rather than a last-minute scramble, the ground transportation plan was strategically re-routed well ahead of the show: longer ride times built into the schedule, with food and beverage service added to the vehicles for the extended drive in for 245 arriving attendees.

"AutomationCON, B&R North America's annual Sales and Engineering conference, is an awesome opportunity to increase your company and product knowledge, learn about upcoming product developments and innovations, and share your experiences and needs in control technology with your counterparts from across the country."
– 2019 B&R Events Overview, Internal Marketing Deck

The Trade Showcase

Hardware on the floor, not in a slide deck.

Coordinated with engineering and sales leads on table assignments, rigging, and shipping so every unit was floor-ready before doors opened Wednesday afternoon.

  • ABB YUMI Robot Live Demo

After Hours

Casino Night, Battle Royale, and the mechanical bull nobody expected.

Evening programming ran opposite the technical tracks: Casino Night, a Battle Bot-style Battle Royale, an early-morning 5K, and executive golf, all built to keep 245 engineers and executives in the room together after the workshops let out.
Execution

Trade Show Specialist & Planning Team Lead.

B&R Lead on the AutomationCON 2019 planning team, running the weekly cross-functional meeting and owning every workstream that lived outside the general session stage.
01 / PLANNING

Weekly Team Leadership

Served as B&R Trade Show Specialist, chairing the weekly AutomationCON planning meeting from February through the show, tracking open items across six concurrent workstreams and reporting status back to marketing and sales leadership.

02 / VENDORS

Vendor & Talent Sourcing

Sourced and contracted the event photographer/videographer, wrote the shot-list brief across five program tracks, and managed the 1099 contract and liability release paperwork.

03 / VENUE

Venue & Room Logistics

Owned the Lanier Lodge relationship: room block, registration cutoff, shuttle service, and room layouts for four simultaneous meeting spaces. When a highway fire closed a major interstate route three months out, replanned the airport transportation around the longer drive well in advance, adding food and beverage service to the vehicles rather than leaving it to chance.

04 / SHOW FLOOR

Trade Showcase Production

Built the exhibitor setup, load-in, and load-out schedule; coordinated freight and rigging for the YUMI Robot with the shipping team; confirmed electrical and floorplan before release to exhibitors.

05 / BUDGET

Budget & Invoice Tracking

Maintained the working budget across every workstream and partnered with accounting to reconcile invoices as unexpected costs (a breakfast add-on, a tradeshow table fee) came in.

06 / REG & TECH

Registration & Event App

Ran registration through Cvent, led the migration plan to CrowdCompass for the attendee mobile app, and wrote the on-site transportation copy for the event website.

On the Ground

The details that don't show up in a program grid.

What Shipped

A fragmented calendar, run as one production.

Takeaways

What carried into 2020 planning.

  • 01

    A weekly cross-functional meeting, run from February onward, kept six workstreams synced without a single dedicated project manager on the sales side. The coordination model was the deliverable as much as the event itself.

  • 02

    Documenting every vendor deliverable as a brief (audience, tone, shot list, schedule) before a contract was signed made the photographer, the entertainment vendors, and the trade-showcase team all work from the same source of truth.

  • 03

    Version-controlled documentation (a shared drive, dated revisions) turned into the reference set for AutomationCON 2020 planning, cutting the research phase the meeting notes flagged as a first-year cost.

Five programs, one shared budget, and a highway closure routed around three months in advance, run as a single conference B&R could call its own.
